excerpt: if (!MYSQL_DISABLE_READ_ONLY_TRANSACTIONS) { await connection.query("SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY"); } ... const result = await connection.query(sql);
sink: mysql2 Connection#query(sql) at src/db/index.ts:437, executed under a READ ONLY transaction with no function/keyword blocklist
guard: bypassable: SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/passwd') parses as an ordinary SELECT (AST type 'select'), so getQueryTypes/permissions checks never flag it, and MySQL's SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY only blocks table-data mutation, not pure read functions like LOAD_FILE(), so it executes normally
dep_evidence: mysql2@3.14.1 (node_modules/mysql2/package.json), multipleStatements defaults false and not overridden in production config; node-sql-parser@5.3.10 has no INTO OUTFILE grammar support so the write-side counterpart fails to parse and is blocked incidentally
why: README.md:19,68,83 explicitly advertise 'Read-only by default' / 'All write operations are disabled by default' as a safety guarantee of the default, unconfigured deployment. The implementation only enforces 'no table mutation', not 'no unsafe I/O', so LOAD_FILE() can read arbitrary files off the MySQL host under the exact default config the docs call safe. Exploitability additionally requires the connected DB account to have the FILE privilege and a permissive secure_file_priv setting, which cannot be confirmed statically (project's own config falls back to a root DB user by default, making this plausible but unconfirmed) -- this unconfirmed environment precondition is what keeps it at Tier B rather than A. Stacked-query, comment-bypass, and DDL/DML gating were all verified robust (AST-based via node-sql-parser, not regex) and are clear/guarded.
contract: Read-only by default -- write operations opt-in via env flags (README.md).
